storage.name: Events
storage.docs: Events deposited for the current block.   NOTE: The item is unbound and should therefore never be read on chain.  It could otherwise inflate the PoV size of a block.   Events have a large in-memory size. Box the events to not go out-of-memory  just in case someone still reads them from within the runtime.

storage.name: EventCount
storage.docs: The number of events in the `Events<T>` list.

storage.name: EventTopics
storage.docs: Mapping between a topic (represented by T::Hash) and a vector of indexes  of events in the `<Events<T>>` list.   All topic vectors have deterministic storage locations depending on the topic. This  allows light-clients to leverage the changes trie storage tracking mechanism and  in case of changes fetch the list of events of interest.   The value has the type `(BlockNumberFor<T>, EventIndex)` because if we used only just  the `EventIndex` then in case if the topic has the same contents on the next block  no notification will be triggered thus the event might be lost.

storage.name: LastRuntimeUpgrade

storage.name: UpgradedToU32RefCount

storage.name: UpgradedToTripleRefCount
storage.docs: True if we have upgraded so that AccountInfo contains three types of `RefCount`. False  (default) if not.

storage.name: AuthorizedUpgrade

constants.name: SS58Prefix

storage.name: DidUpdate

constants.name: MinimumPeriod
constants.docs: The minimum period between blocks.   Be aware that this is different to the *expected* period that the block production  apparatus provides. Your chosen consensus system will generally work with this to  determine a sensible block time. For example, in the Aura pallet it will be double this  period on default settings.

storage.name: Account
storage.docs: The Balances pallet example of storing the balance of an account.   # Example   ```nocompile   impl pallet_balances::Config for Runtime {     type AccountStore = StorageMapShim<Self::Account<Runtime>, frame_system::Provider<Runtime>, AccountId, Self::AccountData<Balance>>   }  ```   You can also store the balance of an account in the `System` pallet.   # Example   ```nocompile   impl pallet_balances::Config for Runtime {    type AccountStore = System   }  ```   But this comes with tradeoffs, storing account balances in the system pallet stores  `frame_system` data alongside the account data contrary to storing account balances in the  `Balances` pallet, which uses a `StorageMap` to store balances data only.  NOTE: This is only used in the case that this pallet is used to store balances.

storage.name: Locks
storage.docs: Any liquidity locks on some account balances.  NOTE: Should only be accessed when setting, changing and freeing a lock.   Use of locks is deprecated in favour of freezes. See `https://github.com/paritytech/substrate/pull/12951/`

storage.name: Reserves
storage.docs: Named reserves on some account balances.   Use of reserves is deprecated in favour of holds. See `https://github.com/paritytech/substrate/pull/12951/`

storage.name: Holds

storage.name: Freezes
storage.docs: Freeze locks on account balances.

constants.name: ExistentialDeposit
constants.docs: The minimum amount required to keep an account open. MUST BE GREATER THAN ZERO!   If you *really* need it to be zero, you can enable the feature `insecure_zero_ed` for  this pallet. However, you do so at your own risk: this will open up a major DoS vector.  In case you have multiple sources of provider references, you may also get unexpected  behaviour if you set this to zero.   Bottom line: Do yourself a favour and make it at least one!

constants.name: MaxLocks
constants.docs: The maximum number of locks that should exist on an account.  Not strictly enforced, but used for weight estimation.   Use of locks is deprecated in favour of freezes. See `https://github.com/paritytech/substrate/pull/12951/`

constants.name: MaxReserves
constants.docs: The maximum number of named reserves that can exist on an account.   Use of reserves is deprecated in favour of holds. See `https://github.com/paritytech/substrate/pull/12951/`

constants.name: MaxFreezes
constants.docs: The maximum number of individual freeze locks that can exist on an account at any time.

constants.name: OperationalFeeMultiplier
constants.docs: A fee multiplier for `Operational` extrinsics to compute "virtual tip" to boost their  `priority`   This value is multiplied by the `final_fee` to obtain a "virtual tip" that is later  added to a tip component in regular `priority` calculations.  It means that a `Normal` transaction can front-run a similarly-sized `Operational`  extrinsic (with no tip), by including a tip value greater than the virtual tip.   ```rust,ignore  // For `Normal`  let priority = priority_calc(tip);   // For `Operational`  let virtual_tip = (inclusion_fee + tip) * OperationalFeeMultiplier;  let priority = priority_calc(tip + virtual_tip);  ```   Note that since we use `final_fee` the multiplier applies also to the regular `tip`  sent with the transaction. So, not only does the transaction get a priority bump based  on the `inclusion_fee`, but we also amplify the impact of tips applied to `Operational`  transactions.

storage.docs: Information that is pertinent to identify the entity behind an account. First item is the  registration, second is the account's primary username.   TWOX-NOTE: OK ― `AccountId` is a secure hash.

storage.name: SuperOf
storage.docs: The super-identity of an alternative "sub" identity together with its name, within that  context. If the account is not some other account's sub-identity, then just `None`.

storage.name: SubsOf
storage.docs: Alternative "sub" identities of this account.   The first item is the deposit, the second is a vector of the accounts.   TWOX-NOTE: OK ― `AccountId` is a secure hash.

storage.docs: The set of registrars. Not expected to get very big as can only be added through a  special origin (likely a council motion).   The index into this can be cast to `RegistrarIndex` to get a valid value.

storage.name: AccountOfUsername
storage.docs: Reverse lookup from `username` to the `AccountId` that has registered it. The value should  be a key in the `IdentityOf` map, but it may not if the user has cleared their identity.   Multiple usernames may map to the same `AccountId`, but `IdentityOf` will only map to one  primary username.

storage.name: PendingUsernames
storage.docs: Usernames that an authority has granted, but that the account controller has not confirmed  that they want it. Used primarily in cases where the `AccountId` cannot provide a signature  because they are a pure proxy, multisig, etc. In order to confirm it, they should call  [`Call::accept_username`].   First tuple item is the account and second is the acceptance deadline.

constants.name: ByteDeposit

constants.docs: The amount held on deposit for a registered subaccount. This should account for the fact  that one storage item's value will increase by the size of an account ID, and there will  be another trie item whose value is the size of an account ID plus 32 bytes.

constants.name: MaxRegistrars
constants.docs: Maximum number of registrars allowed in the system. Needed to bound the complexity  of, e.g., updating judgements.

constants.name: PendingUsernameExpiration

storage.docs: True if the last referendum tabled was submitted externally. False if it was a public  proposal.

storage.name: NextExternal
storage.docs: The referendum to be tabled whenever it would be valid to table an external proposal.  This happens when a referendum needs to be tabled and one of two conditions are met:  - `LastTabledWasExternal` is `false`; or  - `PublicProps` is empty.

storage.name: Blacklist

storage.name: Cancellations
storage.docs: Record of all proposals that have been subject to emergency cancellation.

storage.name: MetadataOf

Consider a garbage collection for a metadata of finished referendums to `unrequest` (remove)  large preimages.

constants.name: EnactmentPeriod
constants.docs: The period between a proposal being approved and enacted.   It should generally be a little more than the unstake period to ensure that  voting stakers have an opportunity to remove themselves from the system in the case  where they are on the losing side of a vote.

constants.name: LaunchPeriod
constants.docs: How often (in blocks) new public referenda are launched.

constants.name: VotingPeriod
constants.docs: How often (in blocks) to check for new votes.

constants.name: VoteLockingPeriod
constants.docs: The minimum period of vote locking.   It should be no shorter than enactment period to ensure that in the case of an approval,  those successful voters are locked into the consequences that their votes entail.

constants.name: MinimumDeposit
constants.docs: The minimum amount to be used as a deposit for a public referendum proposal.

constants.name: InstantAllowed
constants.docs: Indicator for whether an emergency origin is even allowed to happen. Some chains may  want to set this permanently to `false`, others may want to condition it on things such  as an upgrade having happened recently.

constants.name: FastTrackVotingPeriod

constants.name: CooloffPeriod

constants.docs: The base amount of currency needed to reserve for creating a proxy.   This is held for an additional storage item whose value size is  `sizeof(Balance)` bytes and whose key size is `sizeof(AccountId)` bytes.

constants.name: ProxyDepositFactor
constants.docs: The amount of currency needed per proxy added.   This is held for adding 32 bytes plus an instance of `ProxyType` more into a  pre-existing storage value. Thus, when configuring `ProxyDepositFactor` one should take  into account `32 + proxy_type.encode().len()` bytes of data.

constants.name: MaxProxies

constants.name: MaxPending
constants.docs: The maximum amount of time-delayed announcements that are allowed to be pending.

constants.name: AnnouncementDepositBase
constants.docs: The base amount of currency needed to reserve for creating an announcement.   This is held when a new storage item holding a `Balance` is created (typically 16  bytes).

constants.name: AnnouncementDepositFactor
constants.docs: The amount of currency needed per announcement made.   This is held for adding an `AccountId`, `Hash` and `BlockNumber` (typically 68 bytes)  into a pre-existing storage value.

storage.name: Multisigs

This is held for an additional storage item whose value size is  `4 + sizeof((BlockNumber, Balance, AccountId))` bytes and whose key size is  `32 + sizeof(AccountId)` bytes.

constants.name: DepositFactor

constants.name: MaxSignatories

storage.name: AutoLimits

constants.name: MaxKeyLen
constants.docs: Maximal number of bytes that a key can have.   FRAME itself does not limit the key length.  The concrete value must therefore depend on your storage usage.  A [`frame_support::storage::StorageNMap`] for example can have an arbitrary number of  keys which are then hashed and concatenated, resulting in arbitrarily long keys.   Use the *state migration RPC* to retrieve the length of the longest key in your  storage: <https://github.com/paritytech/substrate/issues/11642>   The migration will halt with a `Halted` event if this value is too small.  Since there is no real penalty from over-estimating, it is advised to use a large  value. The default is 512 byte.   Some key lengths for reference:  - [`frame_support::storage::StorageValue`]: 32 byte  - [`frame_support::storage::StorageMap`]: 64 byte  - [`frame_support::storage::StorageDoubleMap`]: 96 byte   For more info see  <https://www.shawntabrizi.com/blog/substrate/querying-substrate-storage-via-rpc/>

storage.name: UnincludedSegment
storage.docs: Latest included block descendants the runtime accepted. In other words, these are  ancestors of the currently executing block which have not been included in the observed  relay-chain state.   The segment length is limited by the capacity returned from the [`ConsensusHook`] configured  in the pallet.

storage.name: AggregatedUnincludedSegment
storage.docs: Storage field that keeps track of bandwidth used by the unincluded segment along with the  latest HRMP watermark. Used for limiting the acceptance of new blocks with  respect to relay chain constraints.

storage.name: PendingValidationCode
storage.docs: In case of a scheduled upgrade, this storage field contains the validation code to be  applied.   As soon as the relay chain gives us the go-ahead signal, we will overwrite the  [`:code`][sp_core::storage::well_known_keys::CODE] which will result the next block process  with the new validation code. This concludes the upgrade process.

storage.name: NewValidationCode
storage.docs: Validation code that is set by the parachain and is to be communicated to collator and  consequently the relay-chain.   This will be cleared in `on_initialize` of each new block if no other pallet already set  the value.

storage.name: ValidationData
storage.docs: The [`PersistedValidationData`] set for this block.  This value is expected to be set only once per block and it's never stored  in the trie.

storage.name: DidSetValidationCode
storage.docs: Were the validation data set to notify the relay chain?

storage.name: LastRelayChainBlockNumber
storage.docs: The relay chain block number associated with the last parachain block.   This is updated in `on_finalize`.

storage.name: UpgradeRestrictionSignal
storage.docs: An option which indicates if the relay-chain restricts signalling a validation code upgrade.  In other words, if this is `Some` and [`NewValidationCode`] is `Some` then the produced  candidate will be invalid.   This storage item is a mirror of the corresponding value for the current parachain from the  relay-chain. This value is ephemeral which means it doesn't hit the storage. This value is  set after the inherent.

storage.name: UpgradeGoAhead
storage.docs: Optional upgrade go-ahead signal from the relay-chain.   This storage item is a mirror of the corresponding value for the current parachain from the  relay-chain. This value is ephemeral which means it doesn't hit the storage. This value is  set after the inherent.

storage.name: RelayStateProof
storage.docs: The state proof for the last relay parent block.   This field is meant to be updated each block with the validation data inherent. Therefore,  before processing of the inherent, e.g. in `on_initialize` this data may be stale.   This data is also absent from the genesis.

storage.name: RelevantMessagingState
storage.docs: The snapshot of some state related to messaging relevant to the current parachain as per  the relay parent.   This field is meant to be updated each block with the validation data inherent. Therefore,  before processing of the inherent, e.g. in `on_initialize` this data may be stale.   This data is also absent from the genesis.

storage.name: HostConfiguration
storage.docs: The parachain host configuration that was obtained from the relay parent.   This field is meant to be updated each block with the validation data inherent. Therefore,  before processing of the inherent, e.g. in `on_initialize` this data may be stale.   This data is also absent from the genesis.

storage.name: LastDmqMqcHead
storage.docs: The last downward message queue chain head we have observed.   This value is loaded before and saved after processing inbound downward messages carried  by the system inherent.

storage.name: LastHrmpMqcHeads
storage.docs: The message queue chain heads we have observed per each channel incoming channel.   This value is loaded before and saved after processing inbound downward messages carried  by the system inherent.

storage.name: ProcessedDownwardMessages
storage.docs: Number of downward messages processed in a block.   This will be cleared in `on_initialize` of each new block.

storage.name: HrmpWatermark
storage.docs: HRMP watermark that was set in a block.   This will be cleared in `on_initialize` of each new block.

storage.name: HrmpOutboundMessages
storage.docs: HRMP messages that were sent in a block.   This will be cleared in `on_initialize` of each new block.

storage.name: UpwardMessages
storage.docs: Upward messages that were sent in a block.   This will be cleared in `on_initialize` of each new block.

storage.name: PendingUpwardMessages
storage.docs: Upward messages that are still pending and not yet send to the relay chain.

storage.name: UpwardDeliveryFeeFactor
storage.docs: The factor to multiply the base delivery fee by for UMP.

storage.name: AnnouncedHrmpMessagesPerCandidate
storage.docs: The number of HRMP messages we observed in `on_initialize` and thus used that number for  announcing the weight of `on_initialize` and `on_finalize`.

storage.name: ReservedXcmpWeightOverride
storage.docs: The weight we reserve at the beginning of the block for processing XCMP messages. This  overrides the amount set in the Config trait.

storage.name: ReservedDmpWeightOverride
storage.docs: The weight we reserve at the beginning of the block for processing DMP messages. This  overrides the amount set in the Config trait.

storage.name: CustomValidationHeadData
storage.docs: A custom head data that should be returned as result of `validate_block`.   See `Pallet::set_custom_validation_head_data` for more information.

constants.name: SelfParaId
constants.docs: Returns the parachain ID we are running with.

storage.name: QueryCounter
storage.docs: The latest available query index.

storage.name: Queries
storage.docs: The ongoing queries.

storage.name: AssetTraps
storage.docs: The existing asset traps.   Key is the blake2 256 hash of (origin, versioned `Assets`) pair. Value is the number of  times this pair has been trapped (usually just 1 if it exists at all).

storage.name: SafeXcmVersion
storage.docs: Default version to encode XCM when latest version of destination is unknown. If `None`,  then the destinations whose XCM version is unknown are considered unreachable.

storage.name: SupportedVersion
storage.docs: The Latest versions that we know various locations support.

storage.name: VersionNotifiers
storage.docs: All locations that we have requested version notifications from.

storage.name: VersionNotifyTargets
storage.docs: The target locations that are subscribed to our version changes, as well as the most recent  of our versions we informed them of.

storage.name: VersionDiscoveryQueue
storage.docs: Destinations whose latest XCM version we would like to know. Duplicates not allowed, and  the `u32` counter is the number of times that a send to the destination has been attempted,  which is used as a prioritization.

storage.name: CurrentMigration
storage.docs: The current migration's stage, if any.

storage.name: RemoteLockedFungibles
storage.docs: Fungible assets which we know are locked on a remote chain.

storage.name: LockedFungibles
storage.docs: Fungible assets which we know are locked on this chain.

storage.name: XcmExecutionSuspended
storage.docs: Global suspension state of the XCM executor.

storage.name: ShouldRecordXcm
storage.docs: Whether or not incoming XCMs (both executed locally and received) should be recorded.  Only one XCM program will be recorded at a time.  This is meant to be used in runtime APIs, and it's advised it stays false  for all other use cases, so as to not degrade regular performance.   Only relevant if this pallet is being used as the [`xcm_executor::traits::RecordXcm`]  implementation in the XCM executor configuration.

storage.name: RecordedXcm
storage.docs: If [`ShouldRecordXcm`] is set to true, then the last XCM program executed locally  will be stored here.  Runtime APIs can fetch the XCM that was executed by accessing this value.   Only relevant if this pallet is being used as the [`xcm_executor::traits::RecordXcm`]  implementation in the XCM executor configuration.

storage.name: InboundXcmpSuspended
storage.docs: The suspended inbound XCMP channels. All others are not suspended.   This is a `StorageValue` instead of a `StorageMap` since we expect multiple reads per block  to different keys with a one byte payload. The access to `BoundedBTreeSet` will be cached  within the block and therefore only included once in the proof size.   NOTE: The PoV benchmarking cannot know this and will over-estimate, but the actual proof  will be smaller.

storage.name: OutboundXcmpStatus
storage.docs: The non-empty XCMP channels in order of becoming non-empty, and the index of the first  and last outbound message. If the two indices are equal, then it indicates an empty  queue and there must be a non-`Ok` `OutboundStatus`. We assume queues grow no greater  than 65535 items. Queue indices for normal messages begin at one; zero is reserved in  case of the need to send a high-priority signal message this block.  The bool is true if there is a signal message waiting to be sent.

storage.name: OutboundXcmpMessages
storage.docs: The messages outbound in a given XCMP channel.

storage.name: SignalMessages
storage.docs: Any signal messages waiting to be sent.

storage.name: QueueConfig
storage.docs: The configuration which controls the dynamics of the outbound queue.

storage.name: QueueSuspended
storage.docs: Whether or not the XCMP queue is suspended from executing incoming XCMs or not.

storage.name: DeliveryFeeFactor
storage.docs: The factor to multiply the base delivery fee by.

constants.name: MaxInboundSuspended
constants.docs: The maximum number of inbound XCMP channels that can be suspended simultaneously.   Any further channel suspensions will fail and messages may get dropped without further  notice. Choosing a high value (1000) is okay; the trade-off that is described in  [`InboundXcmpSuspended`] still applies at that scale.

constants.name: MaxActiveOutboundChannels
constants.docs: Maximal number of outbound XCMP channels that can have messages queued at the same time.   If this is reached, then no further messages can be sent to channels that do not yet  have a message queued. This should be set to the expected maximum of outbound channels  which is determined by [`Self::ChannelInfo`]. It is important to set this large enough,  since otherwise the congestion control protocol will not work as intended and messages  may be dropped. This value increases the PoV and should therefore not be picked too  high. Governance needs to pay attention to not open more channels than this value.

constants.name: MaxPageSize
constants.docs: The maximal page size for HRMP message pages.   A lower limit can be set dynamically, but this is the hard-limit for the PoV worst case  benchmarking. The limit for the size of a message is slightly below this, since some  overhead is incurred for encoding the format.

storage.name: BookStateFor
storage.docs: The index of the first and last (non-empty) pages.

storage.name: ServiceHead
storage.docs: The origin at which we should begin servicing.

storage.name: Pages
storage.docs: The map of page indices to pages.

constants.name: HeapSize
constants.docs: The size of the page; this implies the maximum message size which can be sent.   A good value depends on the expected message sizes, their weights, the weight that is  available for processing them and the maximal needed message size. The maximal message  size is slightly lower than this as defined by [`MaxMessageLenOf`].

constants.name: MaxStale
constants.docs: The maximum number of stale pages (i.e. of overweight messages) allowed before culling  can happen. Once there are more stale pages than this, then historical pages may be  dropped, even if they contain unprocessed overweight messages.

constants.name: ServiceWeight
constants.docs: The amount of weight (if any) which should be provided to the message queue for  servicing enqueued items `on_initialize`.   This may be legitimately `None` in the case that you will call  `ServiceQueues::service_queues` manually or set [`Self::IdleMaxServiceWeight`] to have  it run in `on_idle`.

constants.name: IdleMaxServiceWeight
constants.docs: The maximum amount of weight (if any) to be used from remaining weight `on_idle` which  should be provided to the message queue for servicing enqueued items `on_idle`.  Useful for parachains to process messages at the same block they are received.   If `None`, it will not call `ServiceQueues::service_queues` in `on_idle`.

constants.name: SelfLocation
constants.docs: Self chain location.

constants.name: BaseXcmWeight
constants.docs: Base XCM weight.   The actually weight for an XCM message is `T::BaseXcmWeight +  T::Weigher::weight(&msg)`.

constants.name: RateLimiterId
constants.docs: The id of the RateLimiter.

storage.name: ConcreteFungibleBalances
storage.docs: Concrete fungible balances under a given location and a concrete  fungible id.   double_map: who, asset_id => u128

storage.name: AbstractFungibleBalances
storage.docs: Abstract fungible balances under a given location and a abstract  fungible id.   double_map: who, asset_id => u128

storage.name: Author
storage.docs: Author of current block.

storage.name: Invulnerables
storage.docs: The invulnerable, permissioned collators. This list must be sorted.

storage.name: CandidateList
storage.docs: The (community, limited) collation candidates. `Candidates` and `Invulnerables` should be  mutually exclusive.   This list is sorted in ascending order by deposit and when the deposits are equal, the least  recently updated is considered greater.

storage.name: LastAuthoredBlock
storage.docs: Last block authored by collator.

storage.name: DesiredCandidates
storage.docs: Desired number of candidates.   This should ideally always be less than [`Config::MaxCandidates`] for weights to be correct.

storage.name: CandidacyBond
storage.docs: Fixed amount to deposit to become a collator.   When a collator calls `leave_intent` they immediately receive the deposit back.

storage.name: Validators
storage.docs: The current set of validators.

storage.name: CurrentIndex
storage.docs: Current index of the session.

storage.name: QueuedChanged
storage.docs: True if the underlying economic identities or weighting behind the validators  has changed in the queued validator set.

storage.name: QueuedKeys
storage.docs: The queued keys for the next session. When the next session begins, these keys  will be used to determine the validator's session keys.

storage.name: DisabledValidators
storage.docs: Indices of disabled validators.   The vec is always kept sorted so that we can find whether a given validator is  disabled using binary search. It gets cleared when `on_session_ending` returns  a new set of identities.

storage.name: NextKeys
storage.docs: The next session keys for a validator.

storage.name: KeyOwner
storage.docs: The owner of a key. The key is the `KeyTypeId` + the encoded key.

storage.name: Authorities
storage.docs: The current authority set.

storage.name: CurrentSlot
storage.docs: The current slot of this block.   This will be set in `on_initialize`.

constants.name: SlotDuration
constants.docs: The slot duration Aura should run with, expressed in milliseconds.  The effective value of this type should not change while the chain is running.   For backwards compatibility either use [`MinimumPeriodTimesTwo`] or a const.

storage.name: Authorities
storage.docs: Serves as cache for the authorities.   The authorities in AuRa are overwritten in `on_initialize` when we switch to a new session,  but we require the old authorities to verify the seal when validating a PoV. This will  always be updated to the latest AuRa authorities in `on_finalize`.

storage.name: SlotInfo
storage.docs: Current slot paired with a number of authored blocks.   Updated on each block initialization.

storage.name: StateCommitments
storage.docs: Holds a map of state machine heights to their verified state commitments. These state  commitments end up here after they are successfully verified by a `ConsensusClient`

storage.name: ConsensusStates
storage.docs: Holds a map of consensus state identifiers to their consensus state.

storage.name: ConsensusStateClient
storage.docs: A mapping of consensus state identifier to it's associated consensus client identifier

storage.name: UnbondingPeriod
storage.docs: A mapping of consensus state identifiers to their unbonding periods

storage.name: ChallengePeriod
storage.docs: A mapping of state machine Ids to their challenge periods

storage.name: FrozenConsensusClients
storage.docs: Holds a map of consensus clients frozen due to byzantine  behaviour

storage.name: LatestStateMachineHeight
storage.docs: The latest verified height for a state machine

storage.name: ConsensusClientUpdateTime
storage.docs: Holds the timestamp at which a consensus client was recently updated.  Used in ensuring that the configured challenge period elapses.

storage.name: StateMachineUpdateTime
storage.docs: Holds the timestamp at which a state machine height was updated.  Used in ensuring that the configured challenge period elapses.

storage.name: Responded
storage.docs: Tracks requests that have been responded to  The key is the request commitment

storage.name: Nonce
storage.docs: Latest nonce for messages sent from this chain

storage.name: ChildTrieRoot
storage.docs: The child trie root of messages

storage.name: RelayChainStateCommitments
storage.docs: Mapping of relay chain heights to it's state commitment. The state commitment of the parent  relay block is inserted at every block in `on_finalize`. This commitment is gotten from  parachain-system.

storage.name: ConsensusUpdated
storage.docs: Tracks whether we've already seen the `update_parachain_consensus` inherent

storage.name: Parachains
storage.docs: List of parachains that this state machine is interested in.

storage.name: HostParams
storage.docs: The host parameters of the pallet-hyperbridge.

storage.name: SupportedAssets
storage.docs: Assets supported by this instance of token gateway  A map of the local asset id to the token gateway asset id

storage.name: NativeAssets
storage.docs: Assets that originate from this chain

storage.name: LocalAssets
storage.docs: Assets supported by this instance of token gateway  A map of the token gateway asset id to the local asset id

storage.name: Precisions
storage.docs: The decimals used by the EVM counterpart of this asset

storage.name: TokenGatewayAddresses
storage.docs: The token gateway adresses on different chains

constants.name: Decimals
constants.docs: The decimals of the native currency

storage.name: Accumulator
storage.docs: Accumulator for oracle data in current block that will be recorded at the end of the block.

storage.name: Oracles
storage.docs: Oracle storage keyed by data source, involved asset ids and the period length of the oracle.   Stores the data entry as well as the block number when the oracle was first initialized.

storage.name: WhitelistedAssets
storage.docs: Assets that are whitelisted and tracked by the pallet.

constants.name: MaxAllowedPriceDifference
constants.docs: Maximum allowed percentage difference for bifrost oracle price update

constants.name: MaxUniqueEntries
constants.docs: Maximum number of unique oracle entries expected in one block.

storage.name: IncrementalId
storage.docs: Next available incremental ID

storage.name: ExecutionContext
storage.docs: Execution context to figure out where the trade is originated from

storage.name: Swapper
storage.docs: If filled, we overwrite the original swapper. Mainly used in router to not to use temporary trade account
